FYI, git's `diff.algorithm` also influences diff highlight. I'm a fan of `patience` as it generally produces better diffs than the `myers` default, it's worth testing with:

```ini

```
I'm sorry that both my comments here have been negative - This PR is a great idea using the unused characters to do this and the it does represent a significant improvement. 

However the problem I've pointed out is real and it will appear in real life.

There are two solutions to this:

1. The Add/delete section expands to include the semantic change.
   - e.g. in the change `fmt.Println(variableNoFunction() + "a")` to `fmt.Println(variable(NoFunction) + "a")` 
   - the add delete components are `variableNoFunction(` and `variable(NoFunction`
2. The semantic meaning crosses over the diff boundary.
   - Here one makes no attempt to fix up the elements until rendering.
   - When rendering you keep a stack and as you cross an add/delete/unchanged boundary you close all the tags before reopening them on the other side.

We need to choose one of these. I think if I interpret your replies correctly you think 2. is the right thing and it's probably the simplest thing to do. 1. is perhaps clearer to the user is closer to the patience algorithm and what we had before but honestly I don't want to argue.
Agree that 1 is clearer. Introducing a new "semantic change expanding" algorithm might make the result much better.

I will open a new issue for this task.

issue_context.title: Diff highlighting doesn't always include all changes
issue_context.body:
### Description

Currently when Gitea is highlighting a diff, it's possible that not all code is correctly "diffed", this means that part of added code isn't included in the `added-code` span, but rather outside of it.

This is caused by broken spans! Gitea is diffing the code after it has been highlighted by chroma. This means we're diffing with HTML code, this causes that certain HTML elements are being split apart from each other, one part could live in the "equal" part and the other part in the "insert" this causes Broken spans, @zeripath has made [a excellent attempt](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/14678) at fixing most cases of this broken spans, but there are still cases where this code fails to fix the broken spans:

https://try.gitea.io/Gusted/Test-repo/pulls/3/files

You can clearly see here that the `), xdg'` part also should be included into the `inserted` code part. But because of certain set of conditions we're not fixing all broken spans in this case.

### Gitea Version

https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/commit/03eba32bd91533f090a82b62bd9cffd9e448aaa7

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

review_comments: This isn't right. The return from `diffMatchPatch.DiffCleanupEfficiency` is `[]*Diff`. Each `*Diff` represents an addition, unchanged or deletion section. There is no guarantee that these sections have to be balanced individually. The slice has to be balanced across the addition+unchanged or deletion+unchanged subsets all together. Therefore you can have: ``` + - amIaFunctionOrAVariable + () ``` Isn't this code going to result in: ``` + - amIaFunctionOrAVariable + () ``` ?

In this case, the highlight is just lost, but the adding/removing tags are still correct. All tags are still balanced, and the last `` won't be there, it should have been removed. https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/19958/files#diff-ee527c0c674cb10b21deadb5c08b523a8ff14727234ce3f752685c51d5e46b19R194-R200 I do not think there is a clear and easy way to make highlight still work perfectly in all cases, just better than before.

See the demo in my last commit https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/19958/commits/9cf358b01a089fea78d476d1714265dda5f23204

It's guaranteed that tags in these sections are balanced individually.
